page: Microsoft Azure E4s_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the Esv6 server family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical Intel Xeon 8573C cores with 2 threads per core, operating at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz. The processor architecture is x86_64, supported by 48 KB L1d cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and a large 260 MB L3 cache. It is equipped with 32.0 GB of RAM, yielding 8.0 GB of memory per core. This instance does not include local storage or GPUs, but it is Premium Storage capable.

Performance benchmarks demonstrate strong single-core capabilities, with a Geekbench single-core score of 2146.0 and single-threaded gzip compression reaching 31.25 GB/sec. However, multi-core and memory bandwidth metrics show relative limitations. The stress-ng multi-core CPU performance of 3991.27 and uncached large-block memory read bandwidth of 36.52 GB/sec fall into the lower 25% tier. Similarly, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and software compilation with Clang are relatively weak. For database operations and static web serving, the server maintains average performance, processing 2843.43 PassMark database operations per second and delivering 7.52 GB/sec of web throughput.

The E4s_v6 offers a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8:1, making it qualitatively cost-efficient for memory-bound workloads that do not require massive parallel processing or high-throughput local disk storage. The presence of Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions and AVX-512 instructions provides hardware acceleration for specific vector and matrix operations, though medium-sized LLM text generation is slow, averaging 4.61 tokens/sec. This server is appropriate for relational databases, in-memory caching layers with moderate write volumes, text processing applications, and general-purpose memory-intensive enterprise workloads.
